question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

options.A: The individual patient in a hospital bed
options.C: The medical doctor in charge of the ward
options.D: The administrative management of the hospital

explanation: You've got this! While hospital nursing focuses on one patient at a time, community health nursing looks at the big picture and cares for the whole population. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why does community health nursing go beyond just giving care at the bedside?

options.A: To reduce the number of trained doctors needed in clinics
options.B: To replace traditional hospital treatments entirely
options.C: To address environmental and social factors affecting health
options.D: To focus exclusively on rare surgical complications

explanation: Spot on! Things like housing, clean water, and daily living conditions shape a population's health just as much as medicine does. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which key principle says that local people must be involved in planning their own health programs?
explanation: Great job! Health programs work best when community members roll up their sleeves and take part right from the planning stage. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why do community nurses need to work with other sectors like agriculture and education?

options.A: Hospitals lack the capacity to treat infectious diseases
options.B: Ministries of health cannot function without financial loans
options.C: Health is influenced by many sectors like agriculture and education
options.D: Nurses are required to handle civil engineering tasks

explanation: Think about it—good health depends on food production, clean water, and learning. Teamwork across different fields makes community health possible! [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main difference between hospital nursing and community nursing?

options.A: Hospital care focuses on acute cure, while community care focuses on prevention
options.B: Hospital care deals exclusively with healthy populations
options.C: Hospital care avoids technology, while community care uses advanced surgery
options.D: Community care only treats patients admitted to intensive care units

explanation: You nailed it. Hospitals treat sudden, severe illness, while community nursing is all about stopping sickness before it starts and keeping people well. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h3)

question: During a home visit in a rural village, a nurse has to make important care decisions independently. Which nursing field is this?
explanation: Exactly! Out in the field, community nurses often work on their own, trusting their training and assessment skills to make great clinical choices. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h3)

question: When a community nurse teaches local mothers about healthy weaning foods for babies, what role is she playing?
explanation: Well done! Sharing helpful health tips and teaching families makes you a wonderful health educator. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is being an advocate so important for a community health nurse?

options.A: Nurses are legally required to manage court cases for patients
options.B: Doctors refuse to speak with families directly
options.C: Vulnerable groups often lack the voice to demand necessary health services
options.D: Local government budgets can only be managed by nurses

explanation: Spot on. Many marginalized people face roadblocks to getting care, so nurses step up to speak out and protect their health rights. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h4)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations is an example of which level of prevention?
explanation: Fantastic! Vaccines stop diseases from ever happening in the first place, which is the definition of primary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h5)

question: A community outreach sets up a free stand at the market to check women's blood pressure. What level of prevention is this?
explanation: You got it! Screening catches health issues early so treatment can start right away—that's secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of Primary Health Care (PHC) in a community?

options.A: To provide expensive cosmetic surgeries for the elite
options.B: To replace traditional healers with foreign doctors
options.C: To bring essential health services close to where people live
options.D: To build specialized multi-story teaching hospitals in cities

explanation: Correct! PHC is all about making sure basic, everyday healthcare is right there in the neighborhood, easy for everyone to reach. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why does a strong primary health care system help major teaching hospitals?

options.A: It ensures that nurses never have to work night shifts again
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory testing supplies
options.C: It allows doctors to retire at an early age
options.D: It prevents tertiary hospitals from becoming overwhelmed with preventable conditions

explanation: Well reasoned! When local clinics handle everyday health issues, big hospitals stay clear and ready for truly complex cases. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a major cause of waterborne and vector-borne diseases in local communities?

options.A: Excessive availability of modern private clinics
options.B: Inadequate portable water and poor waste disposal
options.C: Over-reliance on indoor physical exercise equipment
options.D: Strict adherence to universal sterile protocols

explanation: You got it! Without safe water and proper trash or sewage disposal, germs spread quickly and cause waterborne and insect-spread illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is it important for community nurses to understand local cultural beliefs and traditional practices?

options.A: Traditional practices completely replace the need for scientific training
options.B: Cultural beliefs strongly influence health-seeking behaviors and treatment delays
options.C: Government laws forbid the use of modern medicine in rural areas
options.D: Nurses are required to participate in traditional festival dances

explanation: Spot on! People often visit traditional healers first when sick. Understanding their views helps nurses build trust and encourage safe, timely care. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h7)
